rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath follows reports of the afterlife to confirm their truth and explain their wisdom, while clarifying the Messenger’s standing, the strength of his mission, and the Qur’an’s nature.
rows.anchor: bu haberlerin hakkiyetini teyid ve tekid ile bu ahbârın hikmet ve fâidesini de beyan için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After this, there is no further speech; the speaker swears by the things that follow.
rows.anchor: Yani bunun üzerine artık başka söz yok, ancak kasem ederim ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khunnas can mean those that withdraw and hide, or those that return and fall back; the root can be intransitive or causative.
rows.anchor: ve “hunûs” inkıbaz ve istıhfâ veya ric‘at ve teahhur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accordingly, hānis describes something that hides, disappears, withdraws, lags behind, or causes another to retreat or disappear.
rows.anchor: “hânis” sinen, gāib olan veya sindirip gāib eden yahut geri kalan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hanes can describe the raised, recessed tip of the noses of cattle and antelope; hunus is also used for antelope, their cheeks, and wild cattle.
rows.anchor: “hanes” de sığır ve âhu kısmının burunlarında olduğu gibi burunun ucu dudaktan geride

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jawari is the plural of jariya, meaning things that flow, and functions as an adjective or apposition to khunnas.
rows.anchor: “Cereyan”dan “câriye”nin cem‘i akanlar demek olup “hunnes”e sıfat veya bedeldir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kunnas is plural of kanis: it can mean sweeping, from kens, or entering a lair; a kinas is the woodland bed of antelope.
rows.anchor: “kânis” süpürmek mânasına “kens”ten süpüren ve “künûs”tan kinâs’a giren demektir.

rows.speaker: many commentators
rows.claim: Many identify the objects as the five wandering planets, which travel with the sun, appear to reverse, and then disappear in its light.
rows.anchor: “derârî-i hamse” tâbir olunan Zuhal, Müşteri, Mirrîh, Zühre, Utârid seyyâreleri olduğunu söylemişlerdir.

rows.speaker: many commentators
rows.claim: Others take the oath to refer to the stars generally: they disappear from sight by day and appear at night like antelope in their beds.
rows.anchor: Birçokları da ale’l-umûm yıldızlar olduğunu nakleylemişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interpreting kunnus only as the stars’ rising leaves an obscurity.
rows.anchor: böyle yalnız tulû‘ile tefsirinde hafâ vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More plausibly, stars hidden from sight even while above the horizon are khunnas; after rising, their setting below the horizon is kunnus.
rows.anchor: Çünkü yıldızlar, gündüzün fevka’lufuk oldukları hâlde bile gözlerden gizlenirler

rows.speaker: Hasan, Katâde, and ʿAlī
rows.claim: The interpretation of the oath as all stars is transmitted from Hasan, Qatada, and ʿAli.
rows.anchor: tefsîri Hasan ve Katâde’den mervî olduğu gibi, Hazret-i Ali radıyallâhu anh’tan da rivayet edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: ʿAlī
rows.claim: The five-planets interpretation is also said to be transmitted from ʿAli.
rows.anchor: seyyârât-i hamse ile tefsîri de Hazret-i Ali’den rivayet olunduğu söylenmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them kunnus is a metaphor comparing the celestial objects to wild cattle or antelope, since these terms describe those animals.
rows.anchor: ve “kinâs” dahi bakara-i vahşî ve âhu kısmında kullanılan evsâftandır.

rows.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd b. Jubayr, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk
rows.claim: They are reported to have interpreted the objects as gazelles.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan, Sa‘îd b. Cübeyr’den, Dahhâk’ten zıbâ yani geyik

rows.speaker: Ibn Masʿūd
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud is reported to have interpreted them as wild cattle.
rows.anchor: vahşî demek olduğu da rivayet edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: Ibrāhīm (possibly al-Nakhaʿī) and Mujāhid
rows.claim: In Ibn Jarir’s report, Mujahid says some people called them stars; Ibrahim (perhaps al-Nakhaʿi) accuses them of falsely attributing that view to ʿAli.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid “biz bir şey işitiyorduk, bazı nâs da nücûm diyorlar” demiş, İbrâhim de (Nehaî olacak) “onlar Hazret-i Ali’ye atfen yalan söylüyorlar” demiş.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without a metaphorical reading, swearing by gazelles or wild cattle has no apparent contextual fit; at most, their flight from predators might allude to the resurrection of wild animals.
rows.anchor: gibi âhu kısmından burada bir mecaz ve istiare mülâhaza edilmediği takdirde bu âyetlerin siyâk u sibâkına nazaran onlara kasem edilmekte zâhiren münasebet görülmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The planets’ differing motion relative to the sun may matter, but there is no clear reason to restrict the oath to five planets.
rows.anchor: Seyyârâtın Şems’e irtibatlarına nazaran seyr ü hareketlerindeki ihtilâfı mülâhazada bir mâna varsa da bunu beşe tahsis etmekte vâzıh bir mâna yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An oath by all stars fits the context: all celestial bodies move toward an appointed term, pointing toward the fate announced at the surah’s beginning.
rows.anchor: Ale’l-umûm nücûma kasemde ise âlemde mekânı işgal eden bütün ecrâmın كُلٌّۭ يَجْرِى لِأَجَلٍۢ مُّسَمًّۭى [Fâtır 35/13] mantûkunca bir ecel-i müsemmâya doğru cereyânını iş‘âr

rows.speaker: Ibn Jarīr
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir leaves the referent unspecified: the oath can include whatever disappears, moves, and then enters a lair, including stars metaphorically, because the verse gives no basis for narrowing it.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr rivayetleri naklettikten sonra hiçbiri tâyin olunmayıp

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A general metaphor is not warranted where literal meaning remains possible and no contextual cue points to metaphor.
rows.anchor: Hâlbuki hakikat mümkin olur, mecaza karîne de bulunmazsa ta‘mîm nasıl doğru olur?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stars’ hiding and movement in the surrounding context supply a metaphorical cue, so a general metaphor can gather the reported interpretations.
rows.anchor: Ta‘mîmi tasvib edebilmek için de mecaza bir karîne bulunduğunu itiraf etmek lâzım gelir ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The broad sense includes everything literally or metaphorically described as hiding, flowing, and entering a lair.
rows.anchor: Hunûs, cereyan ve künûs ıtlak olunabilen vasıflarla hakikaten veya mecazen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This encompasses things hidden in the unseen that enter the visible world, then return to an unseen resting place, supporting an inference to creation, passing away, and return to God.
rows.anchor: âlem-i şuhûdda cereyan edip de nihâyet yine âlem-i gaybda karar edeceği yere varıp nazarlardan nihan olan bütün eşyâya şâmil olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using antelope traits as an aid to reflection carries subtleties about animal and human life.
rows.anchor: bilhassa âhular evsâfının âlet-i mülâhaza ittihaz edilmiş olmasında da hayât-ı hayvâniye ve hayât-ı insâniye bakımından düşünülecek incelikler vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier commentaries explain kunnus through entering a lair but do not mention the root sense kens, ‘to sweep,’ although the word can carry it.
rows.anchor: Bu rivayetlerde görülüyor ki “el-künnes” vasfı hep kinâsa girmek demek olan “künûs”tan olmak üzere mülâhaza edilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the root sense ‘sweep,’ one reading swears by what is hidden in the unseen and by flowing things that sweep along, understood as angels charged with purification in the world.
rows.anchor: kevْn ü fesad âlemi olan dünyada tathîrât îfâsına me’mur olan meleklere kasem edilmiş olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes khunnas as those who come and go in this world and jawari-kunnas as angels carrying them to the afterlife; no tafsir report was found, though the lexicon mentions angels and the wording allows it.
rows.anchor: “hunnes” dünyaya gelip gidenlere, “cevârî-i künnes” de ondan bedel olarak onları alıp alıp âhirete götüren meleklere işaret olmuş olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given Ibn Jarir’s general metaphor, all the possible senses may be contemplated together.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde İbn Cerîr’in dediği gibi umûm-ı mecaz evlâ olunca

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This oath gathers the changing events in the world and summarizes the opening oaths of al-Mursalāt and al-Nāziʿāt, which warn and give glad tidings about changes in time.
rows.anchor: Ve’l-Mürselâti, Ve’n-Nâziâti sûrelerinin başındaki kasemleri de icmâl eden bir şümul vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing makes rakabaka depend on fi ayyi sura, treats ayyi as an adjective meaning ‘any,’ ma as emphatic, and sha’a as describing sura; it renders God as forming a person in whichever form He wills.
rows.anchor: “Seni muhtelif suretlerden dilediği herhangi bir surette terkib ve tasvir eyledi.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second parsing makes ayyi conditional and rakabaka future: God may form a person in any shape or remove him from human beauty into the ugliest forms, warning against delusion.
rows.anchor: “seni herhangi bir surette dilerse terkib ve tasvir eder, dilerse o güzel insan kılığından çıkarır da en çirkin suretlere kor,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third parsing attaches adalaka to fi ayyi sura and treats ma sha’a rakabaka as a separate relative, indefinite, or conditional clause; it can mean balancing or shaping at will, or reshaping if God wills.
rows.anchor: Bu takdirde meal “seni herhangi bir surette denkleştirdi” yahut “evirdi çevirdi, dilediği gibi seni terkib etti”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All three readings are possible and sound; sura may mean forms varying in beauty or in beauty and ugliness, covering physical and moral traits and resemblance to relatives.
rows.anchor: Bu mânaların hepsi de muhtemil ve sahihtir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The range of forms includes resemblance to parents or relatives, color, height, sex, health, righteousness, intelligence, and their opposites, in physical and moral qualities.
rows.anchor: anaya babaya ve sâir akrabaya müşabehet ve adem-i müşabehet, renk, uzunluk, kısalık, erkeklik dişilik

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Peygamber
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits from Abu Rabah al-Lahmi a Prophetic report in which God brings a child’s ancestral lineages into view after the semen settles in the womb.
rows.anchor: Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem şöyle buyurdu: “Öyle deme, nutfe rahimde istikrar edince Allah teâlâ onunla Âdem beynindeki her nesebi ihzar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report points to a conditional sense in ayyi or ma.
rows.anchor: Birisi, اَيِّ yahut مَا’da şartiyet mânası.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It also points to inherited traits: semen can carry characteristics of lineages passed down from ancestors since Adam.
rows.anchor: neseblerin, hususiyetlerin her birini ihtivâ edebilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report’s third implication is that God’s will, not nature, is the effective agent in hereditary traits.
rows.anchor: fâ‘il-i müessir tabiat değil, Allah teâlâ’nın meşiyyeti olduğunun isbâtıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remote ancestors’ traits can prevail over those of parents, showing God’s will governs varied natures and forms; hereditary values exist and matter, but judgment rests solely with God.
rows.anchor: ana baba gibi yakın ataların hususiyetlerine tâ Âdem’e kadar varan uzak atalardan birinin hususiyeti galebe ettirilmesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One should seek nearness to God through faith, gratitude, obedience, and good works, earning future worthiness and protection from punishment rather than presuming on grace.
rows.anchor: iman ve şükran ile tâate ve hayır amellere sarılmakla olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rebukes people for presuming on God’s generosity; bal says they fail to appreciate that grace and deny recompense.
rows.anchor: Hayır hayır kereme mağrur olmaktan zecirdir. Yani öyle mağrur olmayın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denying dīn means rejecting submission to God’s commands, the duties that follow from His generosity, and accountability for reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: dini tekzib ediyorsunuz o Kerîm olan Rabbinizin keremine karşı O’nun emr ü nehyine islâm

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despairing of God’s grace and reward is disbelief, as is feeling secure from punishment and failing to recognize His might.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın lütf u kereminden ümidi kesmek, ecr ü mesûbâtına inanmamak küfür olduğu gibi azab ve ikābından emin olmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial may be explicit or implicit disbelief; although the address seems aimed at disbelievers, the rhetorical shift does not exclude sinners before this point.
rows.anchor: Bundan hitâbın kâfirlere olduğu anlaşılırsa da بَلْ kelimesi ile atıf, kelâmda bir ıdrab ve intikal ifade ettiği için mâkablinin kâfir ve âsîye şümûlüne mâni‘olmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As in al-Fātiḥa, dīn is considered in both a broad and a specific sense: Islam and recompense.
rows.anchor: Fâtiha’da مَٰلِكِ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ’de geçtiği üzere burada da “dîn” küllî ve cüz’î olarak iki mâna ile de mülâhaza edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, dīn means recompense: returning good for good and evil for evil.
rows.anchor: “dîn” lügatta cezâ, yani yapılan bir işe hayır veya şer bir karşılık vermektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dīn and sharia can also denote rules and customs that set obligations and responsibilities, as in the king’s dīn in Joseph and the prescribed dīn in al-Shūrā.
rows.anchor: vazife ve mes’ûliyet ahkâmını tâyin eden kavâ‘id ve âdâta dahi “dîn” ve “şerî‘at” ıtlak edilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In customary and legal usage, dīn is God’s institution that guides people toward good they freely choose and that merits praise and reward; its reality is Islam.
rows.anchor: Bunun hakikati de إِنَّ ٱلدِّينَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْإِسْلَٰمُ [Âl-i İmrân 3/19] buyurulduğu üzere İslâm’dır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here arrogance about divine grace denies Islam, especially resurrection, recompense, and the duties that follow; for brevity, most commentators therefore explain dīn here simply as recompense.
rows.anchor: bu gibi mevki‘lerde “dîn”i sade cezâ ile tefsir etmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardians are both faculties assigned to observe and preserve every good and bad deed and the observing angels known as hafaza or hafizin.
rows.anchor: “hafaza” ve “hâfızîn” denilen gözcü melekler var.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kiraman katibin are honored by God, faultless in their duties, and truthful recorders.
rows.anchor: Her biri Allah indinde mükerrem, vazifelerinde kusur etmez kâtibler, dürüst hak yazıcılarıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They know every deed, omit none, record all of them accurately in the register of deeds, and testify to them; the previously mentioned pages are then unfolded.
rows.anchor: Her ne yapıyorsanız bilirler iyi ve kötü hiçbirini zâyi‘etmeyerek hepsini hak yazısıyla defter-i a‘mâlinize bile bile yazarlar ve öyle şehadet ederler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Describing the recorders this way warns of the importance of judgment and recompense, for God has appointed honored scribes to it.
rows.anchor: Bu kâtiblerin bu evsâf ile vasfında hesab ve cezâ işinin ehemmiyetini ihtar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abrar are sincere in word and deed and devoted to good; they will be in bliss.
rows.anchor: Şüphesiz ebrâr kavl ü fi‘ilinde sâdık, hayr ehli iyiler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fujjar are those who rebel against their Lord and exceed bounds in disobedience; they will be in the fierce fire.
rows.anchor: Rabbine karşı terbiyesizlik edip aşırı isyan ve muhalefete sapanlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the day of recompense the wicked will suffer the fire and will never be absent from it, remaining there eternally.
rows.anchor: Dâima ve ebediyen onun içinde kalacaklardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The end result of creation, knowledge, recording, and preservation is everlasting recompense that distinguishes the righteous from the wicked, sending them to bliss or hell.
rows.anchor: ilmin, o yazının, o hıfzın neticesi ebrâr ile füccârı böyle ayırt ederek

rows.speaker: Ebû Hâzim
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba’s account has Sulayman b. ʿAbd al-Malik ask how he will meet God; Abu Hazim says a benefactor returns like a traveler to his family, while an evildoer arrives like a runaway slave before his master, then tells him to measure his deeds against the Qur’an’s contrast between the righteous and wicked.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hâzim: “Amma muhsin, seferinden ehline gelen gāib gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can know by inference or analogy the day’s greatness and terror; worldly days of recompense cannot serve as a measure for it.
rows.anchor: onun ne büyük cezâ günü olduğunu bildin mi ey muhatab! Hayır, sen onu dirayet tarîkiyle bilemezsin

rows.speaker: some commentators
rows.claim: Some take the address as directed to disbelievers in rebuke and warning.
rows.anchor: Bazıları burada hitab zecr ü inzar tarîkiyle kâfire olduğuna kāil olmuş

rows.speaker: the majority
rows.claim: The majority say the address is to the Messenger, who did not know the day before revelation.
rows.anchor: cumhûrun beyânına göre Resûlullah’a hitabdır. Çünkü vahiyden evvel bilmiyordu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is better understood as universal to every soul, since each fully knows the day’s terror only when it actually occurs and is witnessed.
rows.anchor: hitâbın her nefse hitâb-ı âmme olması bizce daha muvâfıktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated question intensifies the warning about the day’s terror.
rows.anchor: Birisi, tehvîli takviye için tekiddir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repetition also separately points to the fate of the people of bliss and the people of hell.
rows.anchor: ehl-i na‘îme ait olan ile ehl-i cahîme

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day no soul can do even the slightest thing on another’s behalf, whether believer or disbeliever, righteous or wicked.
rows.anchor: ne mü’min ne kâfir, ne berr ne fâcir kimse kimsenin hesâbına zerrece bir şey yapamaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That day authority belongs solely to God; whatever He commands is what occurs.
rows.anchor: Ve o gün emir yalnız Allah’ındır. O ne emrederse ancak O olacaktır.
